title: Enlightenment, Revolution & Nationalism
subtitle: Global 10R Regents Review  ·  Enduring issues: Power & Its Abuse / Human rights  ·  See Modules 4.1 and 4.3 in Materials

how_to_use.heading: Part 1 — How to Use This Review
steps: Read the Key Facts table (Part 3). Do not memorize — understand the pattern.
Practice writing one appositive sentence using a fact from this unit as outside information for the "Power & Its Abuse" enduring issue. Use Module 4.3 in Materials for the formula.
Complete the Quick Check (Part 6) without looking at the brief. If you cannot answer all five, go back to that day in your 10.2 casefile.
how_to_use.connects_to: This brief connects to: Module 4.1 (EI Identification) · Module 4.3 (Outside Information) · Module 4.2 (Significance). Review those modules alongside this brief before your next EI essay.

thread_anchor.heading: Part 2 — Enduring Issue Anchor
thread_anchor.label: Primary enduring issue: Power & Its Abuse
thread_anchor.question_note: Every revolution in this unit begins with the same diagnosis: power is concentrated in too few hands (monarchs, slaveholders, colonial rulers), and the people with no power decide to change that. Every revolution also demonstrates that changing who holds power does not automatically fix the problem.
thread_anchor.lead: How Power & Its Abuse appears in this unit:
points: French Estates system: 97% of France (Third Estate) had virtually no political power and bore the tax burden for the other 3%
Haitian Revolution: enslaved people had no power, no rights, no legal personhood — and overthrew their enslavers
Latin American independence: creoles had economic power but no political representation under Spanish colonial rule
German/Italian Unification: small states with fragmented power unified under military force — Bismarck's "iron and blood"

background.heading: Secondary enduring issue: Human rights (part of Power & Its Abuse)
background.text: The Enlightenment redefined rights as natural — not granted by kings. The Declaration of the Rights of Man, the Haitian Declaration of Independence, and the American Declaration of Independence all claim that rights exist regardless of race, class, or birth. This issue is equally strong for this unit.

key_facts.heading: Part 3 — Key Facts
key_facts.note: Enduring issue connection note: The Haitian Revolution (1791–1804) is the strongest piece of outside information this unit provides for any essay about Power & Its Abuse, including human rights. It is one of the most historically significant and most commonly testable events on the Global II Regents.

rows.detail: Philosophers (Locke, Rousseau, Voltaire, Montesquieu) challenged divine right of kings. Natural rights, social contract, separation of powers. Influenced French and American revolutions.
rows.thread: Human rights: natural rights theory; Power & Its Abuse: challenged monarchy's legitimacy

rows.detail: Third Estate formed National Assembly. Storming of Bastille (July 14, 1789). Declaration of Rights of Man. Reign of Terror (1793–94). Ended with Napoleon's rise.
rows.thread: Power & Its Abuse: estates system; Jan '25 Enduring Issues Essay, Doc 1 — Louis XVI; June '24 CRQ Doc 1 — Bastille painting

rows.detail: The only slave revolt in history that led to an independent nation. Enslaved people in the French colony of Saint-Domingue, inspired by the Enlightenment and the French Revolution, rose up in 1791. Toussaint L'Ouverture led. Haiti independent 1804 — first Black republic.
rows.thread: Power & Its Abuse: slavery; Human rights: slave revolt as rights claim; Jan '25 MC Q5–6

rows.detail: Creoles (people of Spanish descent born in the Americas) led independence movements. Simón Bolívar (South America), Miguel Hidalgo (Mexico). Most countries independent by 1825.
rows.thread: Power & Its Abuse: colonial system denied creoles political rights; June '25 Map Q5–6

rows.detail: Napoleon spread revolutionary ideals across Europe but also concentrated power. After his defeat, Congress of Vienna (1815) rebalanced European power — conservative reaction to revolution.
rows.thread: A Connected World (cooperation): balance of power diplomacy; Power & Its Abuse: restored monarchies

rows.detail: Germany: Bismarck used "iron and blood" — wars with Denmark, Austria, France. German Empire 1871. Italy: Garibaldi + Cavour. Both unified through nationalism + military force.
rows.thread: Jan '25 Map Q7 (Germany); June '24 Q7 (Bismarck speech — "iron and blood")

exam.heading: Part 4 — Regents Exam Appearances
exam.text: Unit 10.2 content is among the most frequently tested on the Global II Regents. Key appearances:
watch_for: Jan '25 MC Q5–6: Haitian Revolution cartoon (Toussaint L'Ouverture)
Jan '25 MC Q7: German Unification map
June '25 MC Q3–4: Declaration of Rights of Man passage
June '25 MC Q5–6: Latin American independence dates map
June '24 CRQ Set 1: Storming of the Bastille painting (Q29 Historical Circumstances) + Marat's journal about Louis XVI's execution (Q30 Point of View)
June '24 MC Q7–8: Bismarck "iron and blood" speech (German Unification)
Jan '25 Enduring Issues Essay, Doc 1: Louis XVI and the French Revolution

three_move.heading: Part 5 — Appositive Practice
three_move.intro: Write three appositive sentences using Unit 10.2 content as outside information.

moves.move: Power & Its Abuse: Use the Haitian Revolution as outside information.
Human rights: Use the Declaration of the Rights of Man as outside information.
moves.starter: "The Declaration of the Rights of Man (1789), ..."

moves.move: Power & Its Abuse: Use Bismarck's German Unification as outside information.
moves.starter: "The unification of Germany under Otto von Bismarck, ..."

quick_check.heading: Part 6 — Quick Check
quick_check.intro: Answer all five without looking at the brief. If you cannot, go back to that day in your 10.2 casefile.

items.q: What was the Estates system in France, and why did it create political instability?
Why is the Haitian Revolution considered unique among the revolutions of this era?
What was Bismarck's argument in the "iron and blood" speech, and what did he mean by it?
Why did creoles lead Latin American independence movements rather than enslaved people or indigenous groups?
Name one Enlightenment thinker and explain how their idea directly influenced a revolution in this unit.
